props.gloss_en: the mishna: one may fold garments [on Shabbat] even four or five times
they taught it only of one person folding; two people -- no
and of one person, only of new garments; old ones -- no
and of new ones, only of white garments; coloured ones -- no
and only where he has nothing to change into; if he has -- no
Rabban Gamliel's household did not fold their white garments, because they had what to change into
Rav Huna: if he has [Shabbat garments] to change into, he changes
Rav Huna: and if he has none, he lets his garments hang down
since he does not do so every day and does it now, it does not look like haughtiness
'and you honour it': your Shabbat dress should not be like your weekday dress
R' Yochanan would call his garments 'my honourers'
'from going your ways': your Shabbat walking should not be like your weekday walking
'from finding your affairs': your affairs are forbidden, the affairs of Heaven permitted
'and speaking speech': your Shabbat speech should not be like your weekday speech
speech [of weekday affairs] is forbidden; thought is permitted
granted all the rest; but what is 'your Shabbat walking should not be like your weekday walking'?
Rav: one walking on Shabbat who meets a stream -- if he can set down his first foot before the second is lifted, it is permitted
Rav: and if not [he must jump], it is forbidden
the stam's first answer: weekday walking is jumping over a stream, as in Rav's dictum
Rava: rather, here, since there is no other way, it is fine [to jump]
the stam's second answer: weekday walking is taking a large step, as in Rabbi's question to R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei
Rabbi: what is the law about taking a large step on Shabbat?
R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei: and is it permitted on a weekday? [a large step is forbidden even then]
for I say: a large step takes one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight
and it is restored to him at the kiddush of Shabbat eve
Rabbi: what is the law about eating earth on Shabbat?
R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei: and is it permitted on a weekday? I say even on a weekday it is forbidden
because it is harmful
R' Ami: whoever eats the dust of Babylonia, it is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors
and some say: as if he eats abominations and creeping things
as it is written: 'and He wiped out all that existed... to creeping things' (Gen 7:23)
Reish Lakish: why is it called Shinar? because all the dead of the Flood were shaken out there
R' Yochanan: why is it called Metzula? because all the dead of the Flood sank there
they said: since it is harmful, the Rabbis decreed against it
for a certain man ate clay earth and ate cress, and the cress pierced his heart and he died
R' Elazar: 'and put on your robes' (Ruth 3:3) -- these are Shabbat garments
R' Elazar: 'give to the wise and he will be wiser still' (Prov 9:9) -- this is Ruth the Moabite and Samuel of Rama
Ruth: Naomi told her to bathe, anoint, dress and go down, but of her it is written 'she went down' and only then 'she did all her mother-in-law commanded'
Samuel: Eli told him to say 'speak, Lord', but of him it is written 'speak, for Your servant hears', and he did not say 'Lord'
R' Elazar: 'and she went and came and gleaned' -- she went and came, went and came, until she found fitting people to go with
and was it Boaz's way to ask about a girl?
R' Elazar: he saw a matter of wisdom in her
two stalks she gleaned; three stalks she did not glean
the baraita: he saw a matter of modesty in her
standing [stalks] she gleaned standing; fallen ones, sitting
'and so cling to my maidens' -- and was it Boaz's way to cling to women?
R' Elazar: since he saw 'Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and Ruth clung to her', he said: it is permitted to cling to her
R' Elazar: 'come here [halom]' (Ruth 2:14) -- he hinted to her: the kingdom of David's house will issue from you
for 'halom' is written of it, as it is said: 'Who am I... that You have brought me to here [halom]?' (II Sam 7:18)
R' Elazar: 'and dip your bread in vinegar' -- from here, vinegar is good in hot weather
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: he hinted to her that a son would issue from her whose deeds are harsh as vinegar -- Menashe
R' Elazar: 'beside the reapers' and not among them -- a hint that the kingdom of David's house would be divided
R' Elazar: 'and she ate' -- in the days of David
'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of Solomon
'and she left over' -- in the days of Hezekiah
and some say: 'and she ate' -- in the days of David and Solomon
'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of Hezekiah
'and she left over' -- in the days of Rabbi
as the Master said: Rabbi's stable-master was richer than King Shapur
the baraita: 'and she ate' -- in this world
'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of the Messiah
'and she left over' -- in the future to come

nodes.label_he: דבור אסור, הרהור מותר
nodes.label_en: speech [of weekday affairs] is forbidden; thought is permitted

nodes.label_he: בשלמא כולהו לחיי, אלא שלא יהא הילוכך של שבת כהילוכך של חול מאי היא
nodes.label_en: granted all the rest; but what is 'your Shabbat walking should not be like your weekday walking'?

nodes.label_he: היה מהלך בשבת ופגע באמת המים, אם יכול להניח את רגלו ראשונה קודם שתיעקר שניה -- מותר
nodes.label_en: Rav: one walking on Shabbat who meets a stream -- if he can set down his first foot before the seco…

nodes.label_he: ואם לאו -- אסור
nodes.label_en: Rav: and if not [he must jump], it is forbidden

nodes.label_he: כי הא דאמר רב הונא אמר רב...
nodes.label_en: the stam's first answer: weekday walking is jumping over a stream, as in Rav's dictum

nodes.label_he: אלא בהא כיון דלא אפשר -- שפיר דמי
nodes.label_en: Rava: rather, here, since there is no other way, it is fine [to jump]

nodes.label_he: אלא כדבעא מיניה רבי מרבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: מהו לפסוע פסיעה גסה בשבת
nodes.label_en: the stam's second answer: weekday walking is taking a large step, as in Rabbi's question to R' Yish…

nodes.label_he: מהו לפסוע פסיעה גסה בשבת
nodes.label_en: Rabbi: what is the law about taking a large step on Shabbat?

nodes.label_he: וכי בחול מי הותרה
nodes.label_en: R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei: and is it permitted on a weekday? [a large step is forbidden even then]

nodes.label_he: שאני אומר: פסיעה גסה נוטלת אחד מחמש מאות ממאור עיניו של אדם
nodes.label_en: for I say: a large step takes one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight

nodes.label_he: ומהדר ליה בקידושא דבי שמשי
nodes.label_en: and it is restored to him at the kiddush of Shabbat eve

nodes.label_he: מהו לאכול אדמה בשבת
nodes.label_en: Rabbi: what is the law about eating earth on Shabbat?

nodes.label_he: וכי בחול מי הותרה? שאני אומר: אף בחול אסור
nodes.label_en: R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei: and is it permitted on a weekday? I say even on a weekday it is forbidden

nodes.label_he: מפני שהוא מלקה
nodes.label_en: because it is harmful

nodes.label_he: כל האוכל מעפרה של בבל -- כאילו אוכל מבשר אבותיו
nodes.label_en: R' Ami: whoever eats the dust of Babylonia, it is as if he eats the flesh of his ancestors

nodes.label_he: ויש אומרים: כאילו אוכל שקצים ורמשים
nodes.label_en: and some say: as if he eats abominations and creeping things

nodes.label_he: דכתיב: וימח את כל היקום וגו'
nodes.label_en: as it is written: 'and He wiped out all that existed... to creeping things' (Gen 7:23)

nodes.label_he: למה נקרא שמה שנער -- שכל מתי מבול ננערו לשם
nodes.label_en: Reish Lakish: why is it called Shinar? because all the dead of the Flood were shaken out there

nodes.label_he: למה נקרא שמה מצולה -- שכל מתי מבול נצטללו לשם
nodes.label_en: R' Yochanan: why is it called Metzula? because all the dead of the Flood sank there

nodes.label_he: אמרי: כיון דמלקי גזרו ביה רבנן
nodes.label_en: they said: since it is harmful, the Rabbis decreed against it

nodes.label_he: דהא ההוא גברא דאכל גרגישתא ואכל תחלי, וקדחו ליה תחלי בליביה, ומית
nodes.label_en: for a certain man ate clay earth and ate cress, and the cress pierced his heart and he died

nodes.label_he: ושמת שמלתיך -- אמר רבי אלעזר: אלו בגדים של שבת
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'and put on your robes' (Ruth 3:3) -- these are Shabbat garments

nodes.label_he: תן לחכם ויחכם עוד -- אמר רבי אלעזר: זו רות המואביה ושמואל הרמתי
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'give to the wise and he will be wiser still' (Prov 9:9) -- this is Ruth the Moabite and…

nodes.label_he: רות -- דאילו נעמי קאמרה לה ורחצת וסכת ושמת שמלתיך עליך וירדת הגרן, ואילו בדידה כתיב ותרד הגרן, והדר ותעש ככל אשר צותה חמותה
nodes.label_en: Ruth: Naomi told her to bathe, anoint, dress and go down, but of her it is written 'she went down'…

nodes.label_he: שמואל -- דאילו עלי קאמר ליה ואמרת דבר ה' כי שומע עבדך, ואילו בדידיה כתיב ויאמר שמואל דבר כי שמע עבדך, ולא אמר דבר ה'
nodes.label_en: Samuel: Eli told him to say 'speak, Lord', but of him it is written 'speak, for Your servant hears'…

nodes.label_he: ותלך ותבוא ותלקט בשדה -- שהלכה ובאת, הלכה ובאת, עד שמצאה בני אדם המהוגנין לילך עמהם
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'and she went and came and gleaned' -- she went and came, went and came, until she found…

nodes.label_he: וכי דרכו של בועז לשאול בנערה
nodes.label_en: and was it Boaz's way to ask about a girl?

nodes.label_he: דבר חכמה ראה בה
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: he saw a matter of wisdom in her

nodes.label_he: שתי שבלין -- לוקטת, שלש שבלין -- אינה לוקטת
nodes.label_en: two stalks she gleaned; three stalks she did not glean

nodes.label_he: במתניתא תנא: דבר צניעות ראה בה
nodes.label_en: the baraita: he saw a matter of modesty in her

nodes.label_he: עומדות -- מעומד, נופלות -- מיושב
nodes.label_en: standing [stalks] she gleaned standing; fallen ones, sitting

nodes.label_he: וכה תדבקין עם נערתי -- וכי דרכו של בועז לידבק עם הנשים
nodes.label_en: 'and so cling to my maidens' -- and was it Boaz's way to cling to women?

nodes.label_he: כיון דחזא ותשק ערפה לחמותה ורות דבקה בה, אמר: שרי לאידבוקי בה
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: since he saw 'Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and Ruth clung to her', he said: it is perm…

nodes.label_he: גשי הלום -- רמז רמז לה: עתידה מלכות בית דוד לצאת ממך
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'come here [halom]' (Ruth 2:14) -- he hinted to her: the kingdom of David's house will i…

nodes.label_he: דכתיב ביה הלום, שנאמר: ויבא המלך דוד וישב לפני ה' ויאמר... כי הביאתני עד הלם
nodes.label_en: for 'halom' is written of it, as it is said: 'Who am I... that You have brought me to here [halom]?…

nodes.label_he: וטבלת פתך בחמץ -- מכאן שהחומץ יפה לשרב
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'and dip your bread in vinegar' -- from here, vinegar is good in hot weather

nodes.label_he: רמז רמז לה: עתיד בן לצאת ממך שמעשיו קשין כחומץ, ומנו -- מנשה
nodes.label_en: R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: he hinted to her that a son would issue from her whose deeds are harsh as v…

nodes.label_he: ותשב מצד הקוצרים -- מצד הקוצרים ולא בתוך הקוצרים, רמז רמז לה שעתידה מלכות בית דוד שתתחלק
nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'beside the reapers' and not among them -- a hint that the kingdom of David's house woul…

nodes.label_en: R' Elazar: 'and she ate' -- in the days of David

nodes.label_he: ותשבע -- בימי שלמה
nodes.label_en: 'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of Solomon

nodes.label_he: ותתר -- בימי חזקיה
nodes.label_en: 'and she left over' -- in the days of Hezekiah

nodes.label_he: ואיכא דאמרי: ותאכל -- בימי דוד ובימי שלמה
nodes.label_en: and some say: 'and she ate' -- in the days of David and Solomon

nodes.label_he: ותשבע -- בימי חזקיה
nodes.label_en: 'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of Hezekiah

nodes.label_he: ותתר -- בימי רבי
nodes.label_en: 'and she left over' -- in the days of Rabbi

nodes.label_he: דאמר מר: אהורייריה דרבי הוה עתיר משבור מלכא
nodes.label_en: as the Master said: Rabbi's stable-master was richer than King Shapur

nodes.label_he: במתניתא תנא: ותאכל -- בעולם הזה
nodes.label_en: the baraita: 'and she ate' -- in this world

nodes.label_he: ותשבע -- לימות המשיח
nodes.label_en: 'and she was satisfied' -- in the days of the Messiah

nodes.label_he: ותתר -- לעתיד לבא
nodes.label_en: 'and she left over' -- in the future to come
